**The spontaneity of the Lord: the self-aware light**

This is where the whole Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī begins — with the spontaneity, the
svācchandya, of the Lord
text: pilot v1a argument map md dyczkowski mode the spontaneity of the lord the self aware light this is where the whole isvarapratyabhijnavivrtivimarsini begins with the spontaneity the svacchandya of the lord and the doctrine is announced in its fullness from the first lines the blue and the yellow and the jar are not things that a light shines upon from outside they shine forth as the light without abandoning their own being and are one with the manifestation itself this that the world shines as the consciousness and that the consciousness shines as the world is the lord s spontaneity the lord is of the nature of consciousness he shines forth as the whole variety of knowers and knowns with a body that appears as if it were more than consciousness even though it is not more and this is decisive he is aware of shining the image abhinavagupta uses is the mirror a mirror reflects the wall the house the elephant the horse the person the pot the potter all the distinctions of part and whole support and supported cause and effect without being more than its own smooth surface but the mirror does not know that it reflects that is its only limit it is inert the lord is the mirror that knows he shines forth as all things and he is aware that he does so because consciousness culminates in reflexive awareness the light that shines is the light that knows itself shining and this answers the obvious objection then it would always shine for the always has no independent time against which it could fail what we call time is just the sun s movement the shining of things in their succession to ask why does the world shine as the sun moves is like asking why does the blue not shine as yellow it is the nature of the light to shine there is no time outside it that could make it shine or not so the lord is sasvat un cut by time acchanna never becoming other than his own form svaccha clear able to appear as more than himself while being only himself and svacchanda spontaneous free of all dependence on another resting in his own pulsation and so the opening of the work is a prostration the author bows to siva the param esvara who removes the delusion of the world who is the essence of all good the bliss and the liberation and the prostration abhinavagupta explains is not an empty word it is the samavesa the entry the abandoning of the bound knower s conceit the subordination of the i of the world and the rising of the self aware consciousness even the word namah the bowing does its work not by being offered as a bare sound but by pleasing the lord as the oblation s svaha kindles the flame and gives to the deity so the whole teaching is here in the first opening the lord is the self aware light the mirror that knows the spontaneity that shines as the world and is aware of shining and the recognition of this the entry into this self aware siva is the whole of the liberation the work will unfold preserved the blue and the rest shining as the manifestation prakasabhedamaya the svacchandya as the consciousness shining as the varied knowers knowns and being aware of shining the mirror analogy wall house elephant horse person pot potter the distinctions of part whole support supported cause effect the mirror s un awareness as its inertia the param esvara aware of himself samvido vimarsaparyantatvat the time objection and the answer time the sun s movement no independent time the blue as yellow the day of dissolution the four epithets sasvat acchanna svaccha svacchanda and their glosses the prostration as the samavesa the abandoning of the maya knower s conceit the namah as an indicator by the gita rule the svaha and the oblation added supplied recoverable the mirror that knows the svaccha vimarsa synthesis the light that shines is the light that knows itself shining restates the thesis it is the nature of the light to shine glosses the time answer interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the precise force of the four epithets technical glosses the a siva rupa samsarika moha soteriology logged not invented

**The homage that is two-resting, and who is worthy to make it**

The work opens with a prostration — and Abhinavagupta takes care to say what that prostration is. It
is not a bending of the body, nor
text: dyczkowski mode the homage that is two resting and who is worthy to make it the work opens with a prostration and abhinavagupta takes care to say what that prostration is it is not a bending of the body nor an empty sound it is a two resting homage it rests at once in the lord whom it exalts and in the devotee whom it subordinates the words of homage jaya victory namah i bow i worship all move by one of these two directions but each must culminate in the other the victory of the lord to be real requires the devotee s self subordination the i bow of the devotee to be real must rest in the lord s excess the two the exalting and the subordinating are one act two aspects made manifest by the single word of homage before the whole assembly and the attaining of the lord the commentary tells us is the attainment of dasya of servant ness and the servant ness is extremely hard to get that is what kathamcit in some way means it is not a title it is the very heart of the eligibility and it is fruitful of the greatest good for in becoming the servant of the lord one attains the lord s own excess and all the fortunes dasyalaksmi follow from that servant ness granted by the lord s grace it is this that makes the devotee one who has attained all the homage moreover is made in the mind and the speech the mind awareness and the word essence never in the inert body even by speech the text says and by the even we understand and by the body but the prostration proper is the offering of the undivided mind and speech which is the consciousness power itself and in offering that the devotee offers the whole world to the lord as the teaching says he should offer his own self the physical prostration the bowing the eight limbed salutation is only the upacara the visible mark by which the inner offering is inferred not the primary act and so the question of who is worthy the objection arises the eligibility suits the explainer who has attained but how does it suit the mere listeners abhinavagupta s answer is that the listener and the explainer are not two separate undertakings the recognition is one and the servant ness is one it is by this that the lord s favor is won the recognition is preceded by and inferred from the lord s favor and this is where the gita s four kinds of devotees come in the distressed the seeker of knowledge the seeker of wealth and the knower all of them in their several gradations are worthy of the servant ness and of the recognition the door is not narrow in the way of the world s ranks it is narrow only in the way of the heart for what is required is the self subordination the dasya and that once attained draws the lord near preserved the right teacher samyagvyutpadaka the buddhists as makers and haters the kathamukhatilaka the unprecedented prostration the two resting homage jaya self subordination namah lord s excess the jar shines and sees kathamcit the dasya is hard to get mahaphala the attainment of all fortunes dasyalaksmi by the lord s grace vacapi by body too the homage in mind speech not the inert body the offering of the whole world he should offer his own self the physical prostration as the upacara inferred mark the satyam obstacle removal vs the greater purpose adyapi un broken by the book the explainer honored the recognition preceded by the lord s favor the listener not separate objection and answer the four gita devotees all eligible added supplied recoverable it is not a title it is the very heart of the eligibility states the dasya in offering that the devotee offers the whole world glosses the visvarpana the door is narrow only in the way of the heart the eligibility s point interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the kathamukhatilaka reference the exact gradation of the four devotees the text s continuation logged not invented

text: dyczkowski mode the cognition cannot be a thing the dilemma of the consciousness form the buddhist had denied the self but he had also in a different mood offered a reason for the self s lordship by the union of knowledge and action to stop even this abhinavagupta turns the same logic against the cognition itself whatever the opponent says cognition is it cannot stand and he forces the choice with a single dilemma put in the seventh karika if the cognition is of the consciousness form then it must be eternal like the self but if it is inert then it cannot reveal any object at all there is no third option take the first horn the consciousness nature is by its very marker self manifestation it is the light that knows itself and self manifestation is directly opposed to being an object to being manifested by another a thing that is manifest by another is caught in place and time it is here or there now or then but the self manifest light is free of all such being caught if the cognition were truly of the consciousness form it could not be the momentary place and time bound thing the buddhist takes it to be it would have to be eternal and omnipresent exactly like the self and then the buddhist s whole picture a stream of fleeting cognitions each a separate momentary quality falls apart the cognition would not be a momentary flash it would be the eternal light itself the buddhist tries to escape by saying the cognition is not the self s own form it is a quality of the self made by the union with the mind but this abhinavagupta shows fails too for what we call the cognition is the manifestation of the blue and the rest and if that manifestation is only an occasional quality absent when its cause is absent then the self apart from it is simply not manifesting the blue the cognition taken as a separate thing has no place to stand whether you call it consciousness form or a quality it dissolves the second horn is no better if the cognition is inert a dead thing like the objects then how could it reveal anything an inert thing does not shine it is shone upon it cannot be the manifestation of the blue for manifestation is not a property of the inert so the inert cognition cannot account for the one thing it is supposed to explain the appearing of objects and beneath both horns lies a deeper point if the cognition were a separate thing caught in place and time it would have to be held and supported by something but the self manifest light cannot be held or covered by another the covered thing we might say could not bear another s support so the whole idea of a cognition as an object supported by a self collapses and with it the buddhist s reason for the self s lordship what survives the collapse is the light itself the cognition is not a thing to be placed and timed it is the self manifestation which is the self and this is what leads abhinavagupta to the samkhya s buddhi the intellect which the samkhya makes the locus of the cognitions for even there the same dilemma will hold if the buddhi is consciousness form it is eternal if inert it cannot manifest the cognition is not a quality to be located anywhere it is the self manifest light which is the self and the union of knowledge and action far from being a reason for lordship that the opponent can offer is simply the self s own nature the knowing and the acting of the one light preserved the buddhist s jnanakriyayogat reason the same reason for eternality by which the self is eternal the cognition too the dharmin hetu svarupa mutual contradiction the the relation between the knower and the known between the agent and the act is itself impossible and once the relation is gone thence the agent too is constructed the agent like everything else is only a fabrication a convenient construction with nothing real behind it the karika s thence gathers a fourfold absence as its reason the absence of the action the absence of the object the absence of the relation and the absence of any determination of being in any of them and the relation s absence is argued on its own terms a relation would have to stand in both its terms in the knower and the known at once but the two resting thing cannot be one what stands in two cannot be a single thing any more than the two jars in the two houses are one jar moreover the established does not expect another a thing already complete does not reach out for a relation and the dependence that a relation would impose is itself unfitting so the relation is absent and with it the agent that the relation would bind together is only constructed abhinavagupta pauses to make one methodological point and it is important the buddhist thinks he refutes the relation by a bare non perception i do not see it so it is not but a bare non perception proves non being only within a restriction of place and time here now there is no jar it cannot reach the universal non being of the relation to do that one must show a real contradiction in the opponent s own account that the very form he ascribes to the relation is contradicted by another form he ascribes to it that is a refutation grounded in the thing itself prameya nistha not a mere failure to perceive and this is where the purvapaksa the no self attack comes to its close the buddhist has shown to his own satisfaction that the self the cognition the action and the relation all fall and thence the agent too is constructed the whole edifice of a real knower and doer is for him a fabrication

**The self-luminous cognition is never the object of another**

We have seen that the yogin, by the purity and the un-opposed spreading of his cognition, knows
another's cognition. But this draws a sha
text: dyczkowski mode the self luminous cognition is never the object of another we have seen that the yogin by the purity and the un opposed spreading of his cognition knows another s cognition but this draws a sharp objection from the epistemologist even granting that he says a cognition can never be the object of another cognition for how can one awareness be known by a second the two would have to stand in the relation of object and holder and between two cognitions no such relation is possible abhinavagupta takes this seriously and analyzes what being an object really means a thing is an object of a cognition when the awareness assimilates its form when it takes on the form of the thing as the blue awareness takes on the blue this assimilation is the sarupya the conformity of the cognition to its object and it requires that the object be both like and unlike the cognition in total identity the thing would be the cognition itself and in total difference there would be nothing to assimilate now here is the crux a cognition has no such difference from another cognition the difference of place time and form is absent between two awarenesses the difference that comes from the object the blue is not the param essence of the cognition and though the object part the blue or the intent part the passion can be an object by a separate manifestation the awareness part itself can never be an object at all an awareness cannot be spread before itself as a thing to be grasped abhinavagupta makes this vivid with two mirrors two mirrors can reflect one another each bearing the other s image because their forms being of place and time are genuinely distinct but two cognitions are not like that their form is not the place time form of things it is the self luminous awareness which has nothing in it to be set over against another awareness so the object holder relation between two cognitions is impossible there is no perception of any real difference between them this is the epistemologist s own anupalabdhi turned against him and what of maya does it not cover the awareness and make it an object no maya does not really cover the awareness s own form any more than a covering hides the burning power of the fire and even what we call a covering is in truth the producing of a form distinct from the prior state the awareness is not hidden by the world it is the world that appears in the awareness the upshot is decisive the cognition is self luminous it is never made the object of another cognition because to be an object is to be assimilated by an awareness and one awareness cannot assimilate another without the real difference that awarenesses lack the knower in other words is fundamentally conscious the ajada the not inert a self luminous presence that is never itself turned into a thing this is the establishment of the conscious knower with which the vimarsa on memory and the whole ajadapramatrsiddhi comes to its close preserved the yogin s knowledge of the other purity un opposed spreading the objection no object holder relation between cognitions the sarupya as the assimilation of the object s form the object ness requiring both difference and non difference the absence of difference between two cognitions the object part intent part as objects but the awareness part never the two mirror point the vyapakanupalabdhi dharmakirti s non perception maya not covering the awareness the fire s burning power the covering as producing a distinct form the cognition never known by another the establishment of the ajada pramatr added supplied recoverable as the blue awareness takes on the blue glosses sarupya the epistemologist s own anupalabdhi turned against him states the reversal an awareness cannot be spread before itself as a thing to be grasped the bodhamsa point interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the bamboo pillar and jar with itself examples the exact vyapaka anupalabdhi mechanics logged not invented verdict understood and readable v2 c argues cleanly that cognition is self luminous and never the object of another cognition because object ness is the assimilation of a form which requires a real difference that awarenesses lack and this establishes the conscious not inert knower the smrtisaktivimarsa and the ajadapramatrsiddhi close on this

text: pilot v2d argument map md dyczkowski mode the knowledge power manifestation as the very form of things we have examined memory and the construction but both presuppose something deeper the knowledge power jnanasakti the capacity by which anything at all is known and here abhinavagupta makes the central claim of this vimarsa the manifestation is the very form of the objects the things of the world are not hidden realities that a light shines upon from outside their being is their being manifested to know a thing is not to touch something beyond the light it is to be the light in which that thing appears consider the present beings as they manifest they manifest as the outer self the inner standing alone of consciousness pouring itself out as the external world the jar before you is not a thing outside that your mind then copies it is the inner light standing as the outer form memory and the construction for their part do not present a common object as something separate and distinct and even in perception the object does not exceed the experience that reveals it the thing is not more than its being manifested now the vijnanavadin the buddhist idealist agrees that the object is not outside but he draws the wrong conclusion he concludes that there is no object at all only the inner cognition with its blue form abhinavagupta replies that this does not follow the cognition s inner blue form is a reflection and a reflection expects a ground that it reflects as a mirror image expects the thing before the mirror so the inner blue form being a reflection points to an identical ground that produces it this is the inference of the object not as a thing hidden beyond all experience but as the ground whose reflection the blue form is even as the sense organ is inferred from the perception it causes so the object is inferred as the cause of its manifestation the object is real but its reality is to be the ground of the manifestation not a bare thing beyond it and this is the deep point the objects necessarily inhere in the consciousness self by the very re recollection paramarsa through which they are known and the essence of the manifestation the knowledge power is the reflexive awareness vimarsa the light is not a passive mirror it is the self aware light that in knowing the object knows itself the known is not something set over against the knower the knowledge re recollection is itself the known the pure never abandoning the knower being even in the un constructed perception the life is the reflexive awareness so the knowledge power is not the capacity to reach some hidden thing it is the self luminous self aware manifestation that is the very being of the world the upshot the jnanasakti is the manifestation that constitutes the objects the world is not lit from without it is the light the object is not a fiction nor a thing beyond the light but the ground that the manifestation reflects and the essence of that manifestation is the reflexive awareness the light that knows itself in knowing all this is the knowledge power the first and deepest of the powers of consciousness preserved the mangala the 21 verse plan the thesis manifestation as the object s form the present beings manifesting as the outer self memory construction without a separate common object the object not exceeding the experience the vijnanavadin answered the reflection expects a ground the inference of the object like the sense organ the objects inhering in the consciousness self by the paramarsa the reflexive awareness as the essence the knowledge re recollection as the known the reflexive awareness as the life even in the un constructed the jnana jnatr division and establishment added supplied recoverable pouring itself out as the external world glosses bahiratmana a mirror image expects the thing before the mirror states the arpaka reflection inference the light that knows itself in knowing all restates the vimarsa as the essence interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the precise bahiratmana reading the full dharmakirti dharmottara inference mechanics logged not invented verdict understood and readable v2 d argues cleanly that the knowledge power is the manifestation which is the very form of the objects the object is not beyond the light nor a fiction but the ground the manifestation reflects and the essence of the light is the reflexive awareness the self knowing that is the being of the world

**You cannot infer another's mind — and you do not need the external object**

The Buddhist hopes to escape by inferring *another's* mind. He thinks: from Maitra's speech,
text: pilot v2f argument map md dyczkowski mode you cannot infer another s mind and you do not need the external object the buddhist hopes to escape by inferring another s mind he thinks from maitra s speech from his uttered words and gestures one can infer what is going on in his mind the other stream abhinavagupta shows this inference cannot work and he does it with a precise analogy suppose you want to infer the fire in the sandalwood from the smoke if you set aside the sandalwood s fragrance the very thing that marks this smoke as coming from sandalwood then you establish only fire in general not the sandalwood fire the distinction must be accepted without it the desired conclusion is not reached but to infer another s mind you would need exactly such a further distinction the being gone to the other the fact that this utterance belongs to maitra and not to you and that distinction cannot be inferred from the mere utterance the utterance could belong to anything nothing in it by itself says this is maitra s intent this is another s mind and the being gone to the other abhinavagupta argues is not like the sandalwood fragrance a further distinguishing mark resting apart from the thing it is a different kind of thing entirely to press the point he notes that if every additional feature were a further distinction then cow and speckled would both be separate things and the statement the cow is the speckled would fail but that statement holds so a real further distinction is something that rests apart from the thing and the being gone to the other does not rest apart from the mere utterance in the way that would make it inferable moreover and this is the decisive point only the aimed action samihita is the wish s effect a wish produces the action it intends not a mere utterance or gesture that could be aimed at anything so from maitra s mere utterance one cannot infer his wish since the utterance does not reveal which aim it serves if the mere utterance sufficed then even the most grotesque case a pisaca like action in someone s appearing would have to be established as his intent which is absurd so the other stream cannot be inferred the mere appearances do not reach another s mind and this paves the way for karika 6 the appearances alone suffice for the dealings of the world we do not need a hidden external object behind the appearances to explain our dealing with the jar the fire the person the appearance the abhasa is enough and from this follows the refutation of the external object whether it is posited as a whole the avayavin of the nyaya or as atoms the paramanu of the vaibhasika the external thing is needless only the appearance is real and it is the appearance that serves our object action arthakriya the world of our dealing is the world of the appearances and these being the manifestation of consciousness are real preserved the other minds parasantana inference the candana agni example the fragrance must be accepted for the sandalwood fire the being gone to the other as the un inferable distinction the karana viruddha upalabdhi the fragrance not a further distinction the cow speckled co reference samanyavisesa dealing the maitra utters case the samihita niyama only the aimed is the wish s effect the pisaca like example karika 6 the appearances suffice the refutation of the external avayavin and paramanu only the abhasa is real and is the object of arthakriya added supplied recoverable the utterance could belong to anything the crux the world of our dealing is the world of the appearances the abhasa sufficiency these being the manifestation of consciousness are real the conclusion interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the samanyavisesa grammar detail the pisaca example s **The powers of the Lord are his reflexive-awareness**

The reflexive-awareness is the heart of the doctrine. Now Abhinavagupta must show what this means for
the powers — and, first, what it does *not*

it does not mean the grammarian would make speech the pasyanti a separate supreme principle but speech and the mind abhinavagupta insists are only the operation of the ego like the hand they are not opposite the contraction is what the experience refutes the pasu form the word the cognition the organ is contracted the param is the full which the vimarsa is and this leads to the positive account **Action, time and sequence: the timeless that manifests order**

Having established the nature of the power of knowledge,
text: pilot v3a argument map md dyczkowski mode continuous philosophy bracketed interpolations action time and sequence the timeless that manifests order having established the nature of the power of knowledge abhinavagupta now turns to the power of action the two must run in parallel if consciousness s power to know the world has been shown then its power to effect the world must be shown too and here he must confront a paradox that sits at the very heart of his system the lord is beyond time and sequence utterly free of order and yet the world he manifests is shot through with sequence causes before effects moments before moments place before place how can the timeless act in time he announces the answer in the opening verse of homage he bows to siva he says who though free of sequence manifests manifold sequences the whole doctrine is in that one image and the image he will use to make it work is the mirror a mirror bears countless reflections of things before it beside it in all their variety without ever ceasing to be the one undivided mirror it is not torn into pieces by what it shows so too the one consciousness whose essence is nothing but appearance can take up within itself a host of seemingly contradictory forms the ordered distinct appearances of the world without its own oneness being divided in the least this is the action support kriyasraya the one that acts is one and it is precisely because it is one and un divided that it can show sequence at all this is aimed squarely at the buddhist the buddhist had said only momentary cognitions flash forth in a stream with no owner behind them memory is nothing but impression and cognition is either inert in which case it cannot reveal an object or conscious in which case it has no real temporal distinctions so there is no self that is anything other than this flux abhinavagupta answers each point distinct cognitions cannot serve the ordinary dealings of the world a string of unrelated flashes could never get anyone to the village memory is not mere impression and cognition is the un contracted consciousness contracting itself by its own power under the tint of the known object and that self contraction is what we call a power and a dharma it is one it is conscious and it is not inert and its oneness is no more threatened by its many appearances than a mirror s is by its reflections so the first objection the action of the one is not ordered is rejected precisely by establishing that one as the agent the one can be of many natures that is not a contradiction but now a sharper objection order is essential to action the buddhist says and how could order be in the lord who is not cut through by time here abhinavagupta draws the crucial distinction it is the worldly action that is ordered consider the raising and lowering of a hand its earlier and later moments are ordered the single action that is the cause of the hand s moving from one position to another even if in itself eternal is inferred as ordered by the force of its ordered effect so the action of ordinary worldly dealing rightly rests in distinctions and is rightly called ordered what makes it so is the time power kalasakti and this time power is nothing alien it is simply the lord s own freedom the freedom that raises the distinctions of appearance and lets one thing follow another but the lord s own action is a different matter because the lord is not cut through by time his action is not cut through by time either it is eternal like the lord himself in the manifesting of the known and the knower that underlies all our knowledge and dealing the knowledge power is the capacity to reveal but the reflexive awareness power whose very self is freedom in joining and separating is in truth the action and this action though in reality free of all sequence appears ordered it takes up the delimited forms of things in order to reveal the known as if casting the shadow of the known before it it is the timeless showing time the mirror showing order while remaining one and so the paradox dissolves the worldly action is ordered by the time power which is the lord s freedom the lord s own action is eternal un cut by time and the two are not in conflict because the sequence we see is precisely the lord s timeless freedom manifesting itself as order the mirror showing many while remaining one this is the foundation on which the rest of the vimarsa the nature of time the order of place and finally the creation power will build preserved the jnanasakti kriyasakti transition the mangala s free of sequence yet showing sequence the eight verse plan the buddhist purvapaksa momentary stream memory as impression inert or conscious dilemma abhinava s three replies the mirror image karika 1 s conclusion establish the one agent answer the objections the nanu on order in the lord the hand raising lowering example the worldly action is ordered point the time power lord s freedom the lord s own action is eternal point the appears ordered to reveal the known added supplied recoverable the world is shot through with sequence frames the paradox it is precisely because it is one that it can show sequence makes the mirror s logic explicit a string of unrelated flashes could never get anyone to the village glosses distinct cognitions cannot serve dealing this time power is nothing alien it is the lord s own freedom spells out the kalasakti svatantrya identification interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the truncated a pra si 22 and idam ityasya vicchinnavimarsasya quotations fragmentary in this excerpt the precise mechanism of vedyacchaya casting the shadow of the known logged not invented verdict understood and readable the kriyadhikara opens with a clear coherent argument the timeless lord manifests sequence without division mirror the worldly action is ordered by the time power the lord s freedom and the lord s own action is eternal the mirror is the load bearing figure that carries the whole opening what then is time people point to the sun s course the flowering of the seasons heat and cold but in truth abhinavagupta insists time is order itself the vaisesika posits a time substance the samkhya identifies it with rajas the grammarians with an eternal the buddhist with the stream of momentary being but all of them in the end are describing the same thing a sequence a this after that projected outward and called time consider how we actually measure we measure gold by a fixed weight we measure the day by the sun s apparent course caitra walks for a day and the sun s own motion in turn is measured by the water clock in every case the time is nothing but the fixed difference of nature of some appearance the sun the heat the cuckoo appearing as a measured sequence and the power that makes that sequence appear that arranges appearances one after another is the lord s own power time is therefore not a substance that cuts through things it is order entering into appearance the very freedom of consciousness showing its appearances as before and after as a dream or a magician s show is arranged by the one who dreams it but is time merely difference no for then even the fingers which differ would have temporal difference what grounds order is deeper it is the being and not being of appearances what is manifest and what is not order is the difference between the spring that appears and the summer whose appearance is withheld and who withholds and reveals the lord by his own freedom svatantrya he manifests his appearances in every relation the jar on the firm iron the jar and the cloth as distinct or the two as one undivided juice and it is only when he reveals the spring as empty of the summer that order blinks into being this power to manifest and to withhold is the time power kalasakti so order and time with it is not a thing that imposes itself on the lord it is the lord s freedom showing appearances as one then another he is the stage director of the world machine who binds and releases and so divides the universe into before and after the same freedom accounts for place as well as time the variety of formed things house courtyard shop shrine garden forest gives rise to place order the extension and separation of things in space but place order belongs to many things consider by contrast the ripening fruit it is one thing yet it ripens it passes through states one after another that is time order and it belongs to the one the lord by his freedom manifests the variety of actions caitra goes the fruit ripens and so brings time order into being and note where time lives in the known not in consciousness even in a cognition time touches only the known part the object as it appears never the self awareness the pure act of knowing which is free of it here is the crucial turn order the being and not being of appearances belongs to the finite knower the one whose marker is the void thought the breath the body for his appearance is discontinuous vicchinna his shining is not his own form he is as it were inert and it is only consciousness flashing as him that lets him appear at all such a knower is always passing in and out of manifestation and so he is always in time but the supreme knower the one once shown sakrt whose manifestation is continuous and un broken never has his appearances appear and disappear for him there is no before and after time does not touch him and since it is only with reference to him that beings are in time in the end time does not touch the beings either and the same must be said of place the beings of the finite measured knower shine as occupying mutually exclusive places this jar here that body there that is the finite knower s experience of place but the immeasurable knower whose very self is manifestation full by itself has no such division his beings shine in him like himself un measured free of place order so with respect to the pure self the lord has no place order and by reference to him neither do the beings time and place the two great frameworks of the world are both in the end nothing but the lord s freedom and they bind only the measured the finite the discontinuous never the immeasurable the once shown the eternal the world abhinavagupta sums up is the consciousness dense self filled and this the whole account of time and order is the statement of that self fullness and with this he turns to what comes next the creation power nirmanasakti of the thus knowing lord the power by which the one who knows all this actually creates the world the foundation is laid the lord is one free timeless and placeless and time and place are but his freedom showing the world as order binding only the measured and the finite preserved the three rival accounts of time vaisesika samkhya grammarians buddhist all reduce to order the gold day sun water clock measuring examples time order entering appearance the fingers counter example not mere difference being non being of appearance as the ground of order the spring summer manifestation the time power freedom the stage director verse place order in many vs time order in the one the ripening fruit time in the known not the knower the finite discontinuous knower vs the once shown immeasurable the jar body mutual exclusion the upasamhara and the creation power bridge added supplied recoverable a this after that projected outward glosses krama as time time is not a substance that cuts through things states the negative the lord s freedom showing appearances as one then another ties kalasakti to svatantrya interpretive unpacking not resolved the paninian lyablopa sasthi reading of mitatmanah k7 the force of sakrtvibhatah the fragmentary karika 9 text logged not invented verdict the full v3 a opening karikas 1 9 is now understood and readable as one sustained argument the timeless placeless lord manifests time and place as his own freedom binding only the finite discontinuous knower the mirror freedom images carry the whole vimarsa

text: pilot v3c argument map md dyczkowski mode the valid means what establishes and what it produces abhinavagupta now turns to the heart of the relation between the known and the knower the valid means of cognition pramana everything in the world is established through a pramana nothing is known without one so before anything else we must determine what a pramana is and what it yields in the world s ordinary usage the answer seems simple the object the external blue or the inner pleasure by whose force the cognition stands firm within its own fixed limit as this by its own form and of this form by some further qualifying feature that object is called the valid means the blue itself one might say is what makes the cognition of blue valid but a moment s reflection undoes this the object does not stand by its own power alone if it did the blue would appear to me and not to caitra it would shine the same for everyone it appears to me and so it stands by the power of another and that other cannot be inert an inert thing could no more establish an appearance than a blind man could guide a blind man so the other must be of the nature of consciousness yet mere consciousness is not enough either an undifferentiated consciousness could never set blue apart from yellow what establishes the blue is a consciousness tinted by the blue turned toward the blue shining as the blue that appearance abhasa is what sets the blue before us and the blue it establishes is a distinct blue if the blue were not distinct from consciousness then the very same consciousness being one with everything would have to be yellow too so the appearance is the shining of a distinct blue even though in the deepest sense the blue is not other than the great light of consciousness the distinction appears nonetheless now comes the grand unification this whole arising the contraction of the light by the limiting conditions the void the body the rest is one single act of the creation power and that one act is precisely the illumination of the knower the means and the known together pramatr pramana prameya as the siddhapada puts it the one light rises born of means object and knower there is not one power for knowing another for the means another for the object it is all one light one manifestation so what concretely is the pramana for us the bound knowers in the maya bound knower contracted by the body and the rest turned inward the appearance as it were made distinct faces the external object as long as it operates it is tinted by the place and time of the object changing **How many appearances make one thing**

text: dyczkowski mode how many appearances make one thing abhinavagupta had concluded that the valid means operates on the appearance alone but this raises a pressing problem the world treats things as one the jar the fire the gold if the means seizes only an appearance how can it ever reach the single thing those appearances belong to and how can many ever shifting appearances all belong to one and the same thing the answer developed across six karikas turns on the synthesizing awareness the one reflective grasp that gathers the many appearances into one take the jar at first glance it is simply one but reflect the discriminating mind divides it it divides it according to our freedom according to our wish according to the conventions we have learned looked at from one side it is long from another round from another upright it is a being a substance a jar gold a shining thing so the one jar shows many appearances what then keeps it one it is the synthesis anusandhana the reflexive awareness that is the very light by which all these appearances shine sometimes this awareness rests in the single appearance and yields the universal the jar ness that is the same in every jar sometimes it mixes this of this form and is the synthesis that joins the appearances into the one thing it is by the synthesis that the many appearances of the jar are established as one jar the appearances though divided by viewpoint wish and trained perception the smoke and sandalwood are known by a perception born of practice are nevertheless un divided by place and time they all belong here and now so the divisions are not of the thing s being somewhere at some time they are divisions of how it appears gathered by the one awareness now the subtlety of the object action when appearances mix one of them is primary and is the common locus samanadhikaranya of the others quickened by the sentence awareness this here now is the jar the appearances that have attained one own marker ness without abandoning their difference do their object actions some actions belong to the aggregate some are fixed each to each singly the important point it is the object action that makes a thing real in the world s sense and many appearances can do one object action here is the image abhinavagupta gives separate lamp lights do not of themselves light up a single dwelling but gathered in one house they do one thing they make it bright streams falling separately into the ocean with their countless waves nevertheless as a whole do one thing so the jar the gold the red the great their several appearances together produce a single object action say the great delight fit for bathing the image of siva and the doer of that one effect must be one the one cognition the one reflexive awareness is marked by the one object action and what about the fire its heat its denotation as fire here abhinavagupta draws the crucial distinction between what needs nothing else and what depends on another the heat appearance of the fire is un opposed un created fixed everywhere and always it needs no other object but the fire as fuel the fire as cause of smoke these depend on another object the fuel the smoke and the very meaning of the word fire is fixed by convention all of these the heat the denotation are the fire s own form svabhava and they are established by the one valid means the single perception that looks as it were to the glance of the determinative power niyati so even though the means seizes the appearance the thing s own form what makes the fire fire and not something else is fixed and known through the one perception the conclusion of the whole sequence the pramana operates on appearance but it does not lose the thing the one synthesizing awareness gathers the many appearances into the one thing the one object action confirms its reality and the niyati power fixes its own form the one and the many are not in conflict they are two phases of the same appearance gathered by the awareness and fixed by the power this is the distinction and non distinction doctrine applied to the valid means itself preserved the per appearance operation of the pramana the one jar divided by freedom wish convention the threefold division the synthesis anusandhana as what makes the many one the long round upright smoke sandalwood divisions the trained perception va pa 1 35 un divided by place time the being jar substance gold shining word footings the primary locus co reference samanadhikaranya the aggregate vs fixed object action the universal as the appearance mere tinging the individual the blue blue lotus vs caitra maitra co reference difference the streams in ocean and lamp lights images the one object action siva linga delight the fire s heat anapeksa vs fuel smoke vastvantarapeksa the convention fixed denotation the one perception establishing the own form the niyati power added supplied recoverable they all belong here and now glosses un divided by place time it is the object action that makes a thing real in the world s sense restates arthakriyakarita lokika vastusattva they do one thing they make it bright spells out the lamp image what makes the fire fire and not something else glosses the own form interpretive unpacking not resolved the exact force of the va pa 1 35 citation the niyati power s precise relation to kalasakti the karika 8 denotation clause logged not invented verdict understood and readable the sequence shows cleanly how the per appearance pramana still reaches the one thing by the synthesizing awareness many one the one object action confirming reality and the niyati fixed own form known through the one perception

of all if the means seizes only appearances how do we ever tell the true from the false the real jar from the illusory double moon or the shell from the silver it is mistaken for and if the impression there is necessarily the attainment of one s own form the agama declares unwavering in self experience he is called the jivanmukta the one liberated while living but he who still constructs agama verse abhinava s own nothing new established 1 1 2 the 3 colophon added supplied recoverable the order matters glosses the diksa priority they only reveal what was already there states the nothing new point the jivanmukta the one liberated while living gives the term interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the canonical enumeration of the fourfold krtya the exact ontology of the mohakalasamskara delusion impression logged not invented verdict understood and readable the trtiyo vimarsa closes cleanly attainment is by grace through the fourfold effort initiation first nothing new is established

**Causality is the conscious knower's agency**

In the previous vimarśa the relation between the known and the knower was shown to be the very
expansion of the action-power. Now Abhinavagupta turns to
text: dyczkowski mode causality is the conscious knower s agency in the previous vimarsa the relation between the known and the knower was shown to be the very expansion of the action power now abhinavagupta turns to the other great relation cause and effect and he announces his thesis without hesitation the essence of cause and effect is nothing but the relation of agent and object of action causality in the end is the agency of a conscious knower everything that follows eleven karikas of argument against the inert the buddhist and the samkhya serves to prove that single claim it begins with the lord this ancient knower manifests the world of beings without break how does he do it by his will the un divided un ordered will that is non different from him and where are these beings for him in his infinite power all beings are ultimately his own powers this will driven manifesting is precisely his action his making his creating the objection if the will is eternal then creation and destruction would be simultaneous if occasional then it needs another cause is answered the will is tinted by the particular thing to be made and so it is not simultaneous with everything at once now the hard work to show that the inert cannot be a cause take the seed and the sprout the inert seed cannot endow the sprout with being for the sprout is either already existent in which case nothing is acquired or non existent in which case it cannot come to be since the non existent has no nature by which to gain existence the claim that the effect is both existent and non existent or neither is self contradictory the blue cannot become yellow however hard we try so the non existent cannot acquire existence hence the inert material cause has no real causal power the real cause is elsewhere the cause abhinavagupta argues across the next karikas is the conscious the potter creates the pot by his power the yogin by his will alone brings about an effect without any clay or seed if the inert seed and clay were the true causes this would be impossible but it is not impossible which shows that the true cause is consciousness the free will that shapes the effect the whole apparatus of the inner and outer the two appearances resolves into this the effect arises from the conscious knower s will and ultimately from the lord and what of inference the way we come to know causes at all here abhinavagupta examines the own nature reason svabhavahetu it has two kinds in the first the cause effect relation is clear and embryonic it is fiery because it is smoky where fire is the cause of smoke in the second the relation is reversed take the famous example the simsapa a kind of tree from this is a simsapa we infer this is a tree but here there is no otherness the simsapa ness is not a separate thing from the tree ness it is the tree ness in a specific form so the entailment holds wherever the simsapa ness is the tree ness is even though the genuine causal relation that requires two distinct things is absent this is the basis of all inference the cause is necessarily present with the effect fixed by the determinative power and the simsapa born from its own seed by the rule that a thing arises from its own full complement of causes is precisely the simsapa ness that excludes non tree ness the upshot causality even at the level of inference is grounded in a real necessary relation not in the power of the inert the buddhist s and the samkhya s accounts of causality far from threatening this actually rest on the same basis when understood rightly and this entire edifice shows that the agency of the knower which is the essence of causality is not something that could belong to a limited non lordship being it requires the lord causality in the end is the lord s will at work the relation of agent and object of action expanded through the whole world preserved the mangala the 21 verse plan thesis 1 reject inert 3 conscious agent 6 anumana niyati 3 sakya 3 kapila 3 non lordship 2 karika 1 lord manifests by will beings are his powers 1 5 10 the eternal occasional will objection and its answer the satkaryavada existent non existent effect the blue cannot become yellow the inert has no causal power the potter and the yogin conscious creates without clay seed the effect from the conscious will the svabhavahetu two kinds clear embryonic fire smoke reversed simsapa tree the non otherness of simsapa ness and tree ness the cause fixed to the effect by the niyati power the ekasamagri rule the co opting of the buddhist and samkhya theories the agency requiring the lord added supplied recoverable the blue cannot become yellow however hard we try restates the ratie confirmed image the real cause is elsewhere states the turn it is the tree ness in a specific form glosses the non otherness crux interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact three karika anumana niyati scope the precise relation of the niyati power to the kalasakti logged not invented verdict understood and readable the karyakaranatavimarsa argues cleanly that causality is the conscious knower s agency the inert cannot cause satkaryavada the conscious alone creates potter yogin inference rests on the real entailment of the own nature reason and the whole grounds the knower s agency in the lord

**Inference across knowers, and the mirror of consciousness**

We have said that causality is the conscious knower's agency. But this draws a sharp objection from
the Buddh
text: pilot v3h argument map md dyczkowski mode inference across knowers and the mirror of consciousness we have said that causality is the conscious knower s agency but this draws a sharp objection from the buddhist idealist the vijnanavadin if everything is appearance he says then cause and effect are only relations between appearances an un manifested fire is nothing at all so how can the smoke appearance arise from it and how can you infer the fire from the smoke abhinavagupta s answer is subtle and rests on the one creation the vijnanavadin holding each conscious stream to have its own private appearances could find cause and effect only within his own smoke and fire appearances he can never reach another s but in our view this is wrong the lord creates the appearances for all the knowers at once as one so when we grasp the pervasion that smoke implies fire the smoke appearance and the fire appearance belong in the lord s single creation to every knower alike the smoke appearance arises from the fire appearance and this pervasion can be grasped once for all and for the whole range of knowers from the worm to the omniscient the fire appearance is one not split by the difference of streams so the smoke can arise from it and from nothing else that fire appearance being indirect to the one who infers is what we call the cause of the lord adhipatipratyaya it is new not like the smoke that is born of smoke it is the non wandering effect marker by which the inference is actually made so inference holds across knowers because the lord has created the appearances as one now the dependence of cause and effect the in this existing this is that the pervasion expresses here abhinavagupta is careful the dependence is not a real otherness between two separate things the fire and its heat their distinction is only constructed the fire as the shining own marker cannot have the heat as a separate own form both are of equal cause both come from the one reality so in truth the dependence is one quickened by the synthesis by the awareness that joins them the grammatical point the locative in fire there is heat is not meaningless nor does it point to a merely fabricated referent it is real and it is supported by the one knower the dependence of cause and effect is not two things leaning on each other it is one thing known as one but what if the samkhya with its own account of transformation offers a better story here abhinavagupta shows that even the samkhya s dry cause and effect is not dry the samkhya says there is one substance the seed or the primal principle with an ordered variety of natures the earlier nature is the cause the later is the effect the whole evolves by transformation parinama but abhinavagupta s point is that the transformation itself is an action the transition from the earlier nature given up to the later nature newly unfolded is precisely the agent act object structure the freedom of transforming which is agency so even in the samkhya view causality is not the dry change of a thing it already contains the free knower s act the intellect the earth the sprout all are states of the one substance and the transformation that runs through them is an action and finally the great closing argument why only consciousness can bear difference and non difference at all the inert abhinavagupta says is a fixed form it is a known object and as a known object it is different with respect to another thing the blue as against the non blue and non different with respect to itself but the very same nature cannot be both different and non different that is a contradiction so the inert being a known object cannot be many natured but consciousness is different it does not fall into the state of a known object like a clear free mirror it bears the whole variety of appearances as its reflections pratibimba and those reflections are distinct even within the one mirror without the mirror being torn apart so difference and non difference the very structure of the world the cause in the effect the one in the many fits only in consciousness never in the inert the objection then why don t the elephant and the mountain appearing in the one conflict with its one ness is answered because they are in the mirror they do not touch the mirror s own form they are its reflections and the free mirror shows all even by its mere limpidity alone this is its might the whole vimarsa thus closes on the mirror image of consciousness the one reality that can bear the world s difference and non difference because it is a free clear light that reflects all without being divided by any reflection preserved the vijnanavadin s objection appearances only un manifested fire is nothing smoke fire impossible the lord s single creation of appearances across knowers the pervasion grasped once for all the one fire appearance across streams worm omniscient the adhipatipratyaya lord s cause the new nutana fire appearance the non wandering effect marker the in this existing this is pervasion dependence not real otherness fire heat constructed distinction synthesis quickened the locative not meaningless constructed but real one knower supported the samkhya s one substance ordered variety transformation as action agent act object freedom the states intellect earth sprout the triguna the inert as fixed form both different and non different contradiction only consciousness like a clear free mirror bears reflections the elephant mountain in the mirror the mere limpidity might added supplied recoverable he can never reach another s glosses the vijnanavadin s privacy it is one thing known as one states the synthesis dependence the transformation itself is an action the k18 crux in one line interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact four case paksacatustaya dependence enumeration in k16 the full scope of the adhipatipratyaya logged not invented verdict understood and readable the vimarsa argues cleanly that inference holds across knowers by the lord s one creation dependence is synthesis quickened not real otherness the samkhya s transformation already contains agency and only the free mirror of consciousness can bear difference and non difference

**The will as cause, agent, and action**

The whole vimarśa has argued that causality is the conscious knower's agency. Now comes the sharpest

text: pilot v3i argument map md dyczkowski mode the will as cause agent and action the whole vimarsa has argued that causality is the conscious knower s agency now comes the sharpest objection of all and it threatens to undo everything if consciousness is one if all the world is a single consciousness and the difference of things is only ignorance then how is action possible at all for action needs an agent and an object two distinct things but if all is one there is no distinct object for the agent to act upon abhinavagupta s answer is that action is the one will to do that joins the agent and the object the jar and the consciousness are by appearance two but there is a single re recollection paramarsa marked by the will to do the moment i will make this which rests as it were in the other consciousness essence and binds the two together it is this one will recollection and not any external contact that makes the jar an object of action and consciousness its agent without it there is no action even in a perfectly unified consciousness but here abhinavagupta turns on the very idea that the difference is a mere ignorance if consciousness is one and the difference is ignorance then we must ask of whom is this ignorance the one form brahman cannot have an ignorance that is the mere absence of something else nor can the separate souls exist they too would be raised up by the ignorance if the ignorance is called un explainable anirvacya then we still do not know whose it is it shines and yet is un explainable is the speech of a yaksa a being we cannot pin down and in fact the difference is real our cognition rests in difference as it does not rest in non difference and the very refutation that would remove difference is itself a manifestation and so would be difference and so would be ignorance the whole attempt to dismiss the world as an un explainable illusion cuts the horns of the hare s head and plucks the sky flower even if we appeal to the revealed teaching that teaching too would be ignorance a net of illusions and indeed as abhinavagupta will say even brahman with ignorance is admitted by some so this is not an absolute monism either what then of the division of the powers will in the lord knowledge in sadasiva action in isvara this is not a separation of real things it is one action power seen under different aspects the action power in the action is nothing other than the will as the teaching says the three subtle powers dwell in harmony and the grammarians own analysis confirms it the action tattva is seen in the agent even when the other adjuncts are absent and is not seen when the agent s complement is absent so by presence and absence it is the resting in the agent alone that is the action even where no explicit agent appears here it does not cook the agents fit for cooking and enjoying are manifest implied by the locus action is not a thing that happens to an inert object it is the will at rest in the knower and so the final synthesis the will iccha itself is the cause ness the agent ness and the action the three are one act of consciousness the cause does not cause the agent does not act the action does not move all three are the one will by which the lord wishing to stand becomes the world of jar and cloth and all the appearances this is the action power the will of the one consciousness which is at once what causes what acts and what is done with this the fourth vimarsa of the kriyadhikara the reflexive awareness of the cause effect relation comes to its close preserved the objection one consciousness no distinct agent object no action the answer the one will recollection cikirsa paramarsa joins agent and object the genitive joining the turn on ignorance of whom no separate jivas anirvacya yaksa speech the cognition rests in difference point the badha is itself difference reductio the hare s horn sky flower the agama too is ignorance the brahmapistam avidyaya saha not absolute monism the akasmat no cause found the kriyatva not in brahman the himalaya devatatma nanu and answer metaphorical the need for the aisvaryasakti the iccha jnana kriya division as one power the samanadhikaranya the si dr 1 4 the grammarians anvaya vyatireka rest in agent is the action the here it does not cook implied agents the iccha cause ness agent ness action the 4 colophon added supplied recoverable the moment i will make this glosses cikirsa paramarsa it binds the two together restates the joining the whole attempt cuts the horns of the hare s head states the reductio interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact yaksa bhasa speech of a yaksa image the precise force of the sambandhini supplied word in the vrtti logged not invented verdict understood and readable the vimarsa closes with a clean powerful argument action is possible in the one consciousness because it is the one will recollection joining agent and object the un explainable ignorance is a reductio and the will itself is cause agent and action the whole causal structure is one act of consciousness

is niyati but abhinavagupta s point is that this fixity which seems to be a feature of the things themselves in truth belongs to the knower not to the known in reality the lord alone shines forth as this is the cause of that the binding of each cause to its effect as it appears is a covering laid over the reality by the limited knower so too with time and with attachment the whole flux of the mind rooted in desire and envy is the raga covering these are the armours that hide the pure self in the bound state the bound knower the one whose being is measured by the void thought the breath the body is the one who knows the separated objects he is the mayiya knower the knower in the realm of maya facing outward toward the distinct things of the world and the objects he knows are the categories of the known prameya which are counted as twenty three they fall into three groups first the one pradhana the root cause the un divided matter out of which the world evolves in the samkhya manner second the thirteen organs the external and internal instruments of knowing and acting the five senses the five organs of action and the inner organ with its aspects of mind ego and intellect third the ten fold effect group the five subtle elements tanmatras and the five gross elements distinguished as subtle and gross these twenty three abhinavagupta notes are the known in the impure realm but he adds an important caveat these categories the pradhana the subtle and gross elements are not truly graspable by the common marker the ordinary perception of the world they are not sensible in the ordinary way and even their instrument ness is not fitting in the usual sense so the categories of the known in the bound realm are not things we perceive plainly they are the structure of the divided world laid out by the maya power over the one reality and so the prathamo vimarsa of the agamadhikara comes to its close it has traced the categories from the sivatattva the body of all down through the pure group and into the impure realm where the self is covered by the kancukas and the world is divided into the twenty three categories of the known all of it in the end is the one consciousness woven warp and woof hidden from the bound knower by the coverings that are themselves in truth aspects of the knower rather than of the things this sets the stage for the next vimarsa which will analyze the bound and the lord pasu and pati in their full distinction preserved the kancukas niyati kala raga vidya kala the i ness in the non self the niyati as the fixing of cause to effect seed sprout clay pot the niyati belongs to the knower not the known matrabhasanadvarena the raga as the mind flux rooted in attachment the sunyadi bound knower knowing the separated objects the twenty three fold known one pradhana thirteen organs ten fold effect the gross subtle distinction the un sensible ness of the pradhana and the un fitting instrument ness the 1 colophon added supplied recoverable the armours or coverings glosses kancuka in the bound state the one flavored reality is seen as divided states k8 this is the mayiya knower facing outward glosses the sunyadi knower interpretive unpacking not new doctrine not resolved the exact thirteen organ count samkhya enumeration presupposed the detail is in the vivrti the precise mechanism of karika 8 logged not invented verdict understood and readable the prathamo vimarsa of the agamadhikara closes cleanly the pure self is covered by the kancukas which belong to the knower not the known the bound knower knows the divided world and the known is the twenty three fold pradhana thirteen organs ten fold effect setting up the pasu pati analysis to come

recognition of the lord in the self and to recognize him we must understand the knowers themselves for there are many knowers from the bound to the pure and they are distinguished by the stains that bind them abhinavagupta opens this vimarsa with a homage to the one who wields the trident cutting the three nooses and those three nooses are the three stains mala that will occupy him throughout the stain of finitude anava the stain of objectivity mayiya and the stain of action karma the knower states have their presiding deities in the pure state where the knower stands in his mere knower ness the objects withdrawn the presider is rudra the supreme siva who as the lord brings his worshippers into that state and who even within the realm of maya is the one with the opened third eye but in the spread of the distinct world the presiders are brahma and visnu brahma in the production of the spread visnu in its flowing continuation and the difference is this these two make the this the object primary and the i the knower essence subordinate whereas the pure rudra makes the i primary they are not third eyed as the rudra is yet even these brahma and visnu forms are not something apart from the lord they shine as the qualities of the intellect not as the pure consciousness itself their form is the lordship the freedom the knowledge the action power standing as the support of the world now the bound knower he is the one blind by maya wandering in samsara bound by his actions this is the pasu the animal the knower who has lost his freedom and over against him stands the pati the lord the knower whose own members the beings of the world are his own the bound one is bound because he has suffered the loss of freedom of the awareness he has become un aware of his own freedom and so he is caught in the objects this is the working of the maya the manifestation of the distinct known the world spread out as other than the self which gives us birth and enjoyment and which is the mayiya stain the knowers come in grades there are the pure ones those who even in the unity of the awareness marker are mutually distinct and who lack the highest agency these are the vidyesvara group there are the pralayakala the dissolved ones absorbed in the state of dissolution who have only the stain of finitude their form the un awareness of the void and the rest and even the aware ones who possess agency still stand in the stain of action indeed all the becoming ones the gods and men and the rest have the three fold stain finitude objectivity action and binding them all is the kala the limited agency which raises the consciousness essence into the narrow form of the individual agent so the picture is complete beneath the lord who is free and whole lie the many knowers bound each by his stain the finitude that shrinks the infinite self into a single soul the maya that spreads the world out as other and the action that keeps the soul bound in the round of birth and enjoyment it is these three nooses that the trident bearing lord cuts and to understand how they are cut how the bound knower can be released into the recognition of his own lordship abhinavagupta will turn next snippet:
**The closing sum: the recognition, and the end of the whole teaching**

We come to the end. This final vimarśa of the Īśvarapratyabhijñāvivṛtivimarśinī is the closing sum — the
drawing together of everything that has go
text: the closing sum the recognition and the end of the whole teaching we come to the end this final vimarsa of the isvarapratyabhijnavivrtivimarsini is the closing sum the drawing together of everything that has gone before and its theme is fittingly the transmission of the teaching itself it comes from the guru from the sastra and from the self the whole teaching the self manifest essence established by the knowledge and the action aided by reason has been given part of it comes from the self svatah part from the sastra sastratah and part must come from the guru gurutah for even the vision of the sastra must be carried to its proper power by the lineage of teachers and here abhinavagupta is stern the book studied knowledges without the guru order he warns practicing and teaching ripen long in hell the teaching must be received from the living line from the adi srikanthanatha down through durvasa and tryambakaditya the mental sons who carry the un precedented effort less word and now the path itself abhinavagupta presents it as a new well fitted path spoken by the great gurus in the sivadrsti it is the path of the recognition since liberation is from the recognition alone all the elaborate effort yogas are useless here this is the clear means effort less un undertaken yet bearing the great fruit the breath controls and the rest are artificial the un made reality does not yield to a sixteenth part of such effort even the proud fancies of the bound i am the king i have slain my enemy are when examined still other dependent riding on the lord s power the recognition cuts through all of it and its fruit is the while living liberated the jivanmukta the one who even in the body is already free and who at the fall of the body is simply the supreme lord this abhinavagupta says is the most wondrous thing of all liberation in this very life the closing sum puts it in a beautiful image the lover stands near sought by the slender woman but as long as he is not recognized he cannot be enjoyed so the world lord always present always near is not experienced in his own splendor until the recognition arises the world has him before it and yet does not see him until the single act of recognition turns the un known nearness into the joy of union one who knows only the mere flash of recognition gains the bliss one who cultivates it gains the thousand fold embrace and this recognition abhinavagupta reminds us was established for the world by utpala the sun rise son for the effort less establishment of all people not by caste or conduct but by the very fact of being born a knower through it all beings are graced and by it the author himself is complete the whole teaching the lord s recognition is here gathered and handed on the closing vimarsa then turns to the author s own lineage the vivrtikara s seventeen verses of praise they trace the line varaha gupta the cukhulaka father of bhutiraja bhutiraja himself hatitalaksmanagupta the maker of the sastra the guru of abhinava the tryambaka with its three powers and the method of the recognition throughout the final verses praise the supreme lord and hand the work to him the lord recognition from the reflective awareness of the lord may he make it the one minding the self s reflection and then the two colophons close the entire work the all conclusion the fourth vimarsa and completed this the isvarapratyabhijnavivrtivimarsini the composition of the abhinavagupta foots whose fame is won by meditation on the feet of tri nayana so ends the greatest work of abhinavagupta the vivrtivimarsini on the recognition of the lord it has traced across four adhikaras the knowledge and the action of consciousness the categories of the world the knowers and the stains the bond and the liberation and it closes where it began the own self of all beings is the one lord and the recognition of this received from the guru the sastra and the self is the whole of liberation the book ends and the recognition begins

[chunk-j-k1-11-kartapi-kalpita-v10] **"Thence the agent too is constructed"**

The Buddhist's attack has been relentless. He has denied the self, denied the cognition, denied the
action. Now he completes it. For what hol
text: chunk j k1 11 kartapi kalpita v10 thence the agent too is constructed the buddhist s attack has been relentless he has denied the self denied the cognition denied the action now he completes it for what holds all these together the relation between the knower and the known between the agent and the act is itself impossible and once the relation is gone thence the agent too is constructed the agent like everything else is only a fabrication a convenient construction with nothing real behind it the karika s thence gathers a fourfold absence as its reason the absence of the action the absence of the object the absence of the relation and the absence of any determination of being in any of them and the relation s absence is argued on its own terms a relation would have to stand in both its terms in the knower and the known at once but the two resting thing cannot be one what stands in two cannot be a single thing any more than the two jars in the two houses are one jar moreover the established does not expect another a thing already complete does not reach out for a relation and the dependence that a relation would impose is itself unfitting so the relation is absent and with it the agent that the relation would bind together is only constructed abhinavagupta pauses to make one methodological point and it is important the buddhist thinks he refutes the relation by a bare non perception i do not see it so it is not but a bare non perception proves non being only within a restriction of place and time here now there is no jar it cannot reach the universal non being of the relation to do that one must show a real contradiction in the opponent s own account that the very form he ascribes to the relation is contradicted by another form he ascribes to it that is a refutation grounded in the thing itself prameya nistha not a mere failure to perceive and this is where the purvapaksa the no self attack comes to its close the buddhist has shown to his own satisfaction that the self the cognition the action and the relation all fall and thence the agent too is constructed the whole edifice of a real knower and doer is for him a fabrication
